title: Jury awards male surgical technician $105K for delivery room discrimination
summary: According to the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, two female obstetricians barred the technician from performing his job because of his sex.

title: Fintech company violated NLRA when it fired worker for LinkedIn post, judge finds
summary: The worker posted on LinkedIn that Apex Fintech Solutions “allowed outright hate to proliferate as a demonstration of what they think DEI is.”

title: Why manager training may be the key to AI integration
summary: Without effective managers, companies may have a hard time seeing the gains that they expect from AI investments.

title: Managers say they don’t feel ready to lead an AI-fluent workforce
summary: Many companies aren’t providing the necessary training to help employees learn how to use artificial intelligence, per Indeed research.

title: How to make sure front-line managers are heard
summary: Despite knowing how important front-line managers are, employers often ignore their feedback, a study showed.

title: Gap Inc. opens creator program to employees
summary: Corporate, distribution and store staff can now apply to be influencers for the retailer’s brand portfolio, almost a year after the program’s launch.

title: Previous vaccinations shouldn’t bar worker’s religious vaccine exemption request, 9th Circuit says
summary: An employer’s initial approval of a COVID-19 vaccine mandate exemption request showed that it understood the request’s religious nature, per the 9th Circuit.

title: Court strikes down NLRB ‘successor bar’ rule using post-Chevron analysis
summary: The rule that requires acquiring companies to bargain with incumbent unions exceeded the agency’s statutory authority, a 2-1 majority of the D.C. Circuit held.

title: Week in review: Federal HR office lost over 1,000 workers in one year
summary: We’re rounding up last week’s top stories, including the percentage of workers who see work as a “situationship.”

title: Leadership readiness lags behind AI adoption rate
summary: Only 3% of leaders are prepared to steer the ship on artificial intelligence adoption, research suggests.
